correctness.rationale: For fixed p in (0,1/2), write u=p−t_R, delta=C−R, A=p(1−p), L=log((1−p)/p). Derivatives give delta=Lu+u²/(2A)+(1−2p)u³/(6A²)+O(u⁴) and D(p−u||p)=u²/(2A)+(1−2p)u³/(6A²)+O(u⁴). Since L>0, u=delta/L−delta²/(2AL³)+O(delta³), giving the stated converse coefficient. As an independent check of the optimization, set q_s=p^(1+s)/[(1−p)^(1+s)+p^(1+s)]. The derivative of the negative log partition function is the cross-entropy C+L(q_s−p), strictly decreasing in s. At s=0 it is C, and at s=1 it is strictly less than C, so for all sufficiently small positive delta the unique optimizer is interior and has q_s=p−delta/L exactly. At that optimizer the objective equals D(q_s||p) by the tilt identity. Its cubic coefficient is (1−2p)/(6A²L³). Subtraction and division by the common leading quadratic term verify both gap formulas and their positive coefficients. Theorem 3 of the cited paper verifies the worst-phase converse interpretation; its Eq. (9) is the aware achievable benchmark.
residual_risks: This is an expansion of the difference from a particular converse bound, not an equality for the unknown true reliability penalty. The calculation is local at fixed p and gives no endpoint-uniformity or low-rate conclusion.

value.rationale: The prior strict separation and the known dispersion scale do not quantify how the exhibited penalty disappears near capacity. The calculation shows the leading quadratic scale of the aware benchmark survives in this converse and cannot expose its penalty; the cubic coefficient is the first quantitative separation and gives a corresponding explicit asymptotic lower bound on the actual penalty. This resolves a motivated precision question for the source's concrete counterexample, rather than calculating an arbitrary higher-order term.
residual_risks: A sharper phase-uniform converse or matching achievability could change what is known about the true penalty; the actual leading order is not established here.
